title: Add a make install target so local installs don't use cp

description:
## What

The Makefile has no `install` target, so installing a locally-built `story`
means copying the binary by hand. The obvious hand-rolled command —
`cp target/release/story ~/.local/bin/story` — is a footgun that produces a
binary macOS refuses to execute.

## Why it breaks

macOS invalidates a Mach-O's cached code-signing state when the file's contents
are rewritten **in place**. `cp` truncates and rewrites the destination, keeping
the same inode. If any live process still has that inode mapped — e.g. a
long-running `story web --serve` — every subsequent `exec` of that path dies
with SIGKILL (exit 137), even though the bytes on disk are correct and
`codesign -v` passes.

Verified on macOS 26.5.2, 2026-07-25:

    cp release/story ./story          # inode 549887163
    ./story web --serve &             # holds it mapped
    cp debug/story ./story            # inode 549887163 — unchanged
    ./story --version                 # exit 137

    install -m 755 debug/story ./story  # inode 549887171 — fresh
    ./story --version                   # exit 0, holder process unaffected

The failure is confusing out of proportion to its cause: the binary hashes
identically to a known-good build and passes signature verification, so nothing
about the symptom points at the copy mechanism.

## Extent

Hit on 2026-07-25 while diagnosing [[SH-54]]: `~/.local/bin/story` returned 137
for every subcommand while `target/release/story` — byte-identical, same
SHA-256 — ran fine.

`install.sh:54` already does the right thing (`install -m 755`). Only the
hand-copy path is affected, which is exactly the path a developer takes when
iterating locally.

## Fix

Add a `make install` target that builds release and installs via `install(1)`,
honouring `install.sh`'s `STORYHOOK_INSTALL_DIR` convention so both entry points
agree on where the binary goes. Comment the target with *why* it is not `cp`, so
the constraint survives future edits.

## Note

`make install` does not restart a running `story web --serve`. The daemon keeps
its old mapping and continues serving stale code until restarted — the
proximate trigger for [[SH-54]].
